introduction: This intermediate tier transitions to the hard pedagogical data. It details the exact 'Lakshyas' (learning targets) for each grade, the three developmental goals defined by the framework, and the sub-components of literacy and numeracy.

core_concepts.title: The 3 Developmental Goals of NIPUN
core_concepts.description:
The mission aligns FLN with the holistic development of the child, categorizing learning outcomes into three specific goals:
- Goal 1 (HW): Children maintain good Health and Well-being.
- Goal 2 (EC): Children become Effective Communicators.
- Goal 3 (IL): Children become Involved Learners and connect with their immediate environment.

core_concepts.title: NIPUN Lakshyas (Grade-Wise Literacy Targets)
core_concepts.description:
- Balvatika: Read simple words comprising 2 to 3 alphabets.
- Grade 1: Read small sentences consisting of at least 4-5 simple words.
- Grade 2: Read with meaning at a speed of **45 to 60 words per minute**.
- Grade 3: Read with meaning at a speed of at least **60 words per minute**.

core_concepts.title: NIPUN Lakshyas (Grade-Wise Numeracy Targets)
core_concepts.description:
- Balvatika: Recognize and read numerals up to 10.
- Grade 1: Read and write numbers up to 99. Perform simple addition and subtraction up to 9.
- Grade 2: Read and write numbers up to 999. Subtract two-digit numbers up to 99.
- Grade 3: Read and write numbers up to **9999**. Solve simple daily life problems using addition, subtraction, and simple **multiplication**.

core_concepts.title: Components of FLN
core_concepts.description:
Teachers must understand that literacy and numeracy are not single skills, but composites:
1. Foundational Literacy: Includes Phonological Awareness (sound recognition), Decoding (associating letters with sounds), Reading Fluency, Reading Comprehension, and Writing.
2. Foundational Numeracy: Includes Pre-number concepts (big/small, tall/short), Number sense, Operations on numbers, Shapes and Spatial understanding, Measurement, and Data Handling.

important_entities.name: Play-Based Pedagogy
important_entities.key_fact: The mandated teaching style for the Foundational Stage.
important_entities.significance: NIPUN completely rejects rote memorization, repetitive writing of alphabets, and silent sitting. It mandates that FLN must be achieved through toys, games, storytelling, and experiential activities. Learning must be joyful and stress-free.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: A highly specific metric tested in KVS and DSSSB: By the end of Grade 3, a child must be able to read with comprehension at a minimum speed of **60 words per minute**. If an option says '60 words per minute WITHOUT understanding', it is incorrect. Comprehension is mandatory.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: To remember the 3 Goals: Health (Well-being/HW), Speech (Effective Communicators/EC), Reach (Involved Learners connecting with environment/IL).

exam_strategy_tips: Whenever a question asks to identify the highest mathematical competency required by NIPUN Bharat at the end of Grade 3, the correct answer is solving simple real-life problems using **Multiplication** alongside numbers up to 9999. Division is introduced later.
